headline_marked: [[AI agents]] deploy serverless APIs on AWS in minutes
headline: AI agents deploy serverless APIs on AWS in minutes
summary: An AI coding agent was used to create a Python API with Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and DynamoDB, demonstrating a faster path from idea to deployment.
details: AI coding agents are streamlining the process of turning ideas into functional code. The new AWS experience integrates these agents directly with AWS projects, automatically configuring necessary tools and managing permissions for created resources.

In a demonstration, an AI agent was prompted to create a serverless Python API. This API utilizes Amazon API Gateway for the public endpoint, AWS Lambda for request handling, and Amazon DynamoDB for state management, ensuring atomic updates to prevent data conflicts during concurrent requests.

Before deployment, the agent presented a detailed architecture proposal, including the GET /counter endpoint for atomic increment operations, conservative throttling, a least-privilege IAM role, and logging configurations. It also planned for deployment via an AWS CloudFormation stack.

The agent confirmed that no AWS resources were altered without approval and requested explicit consent for the architecture and public endpoint. Upon approval, it deployed the serverless-counter-api CloudFormation stack in us-east-2.

The deployed API was tested by invoking the endpoint multiple times, each call returning an incremented value stored in DynamoDB. This confirmed the service was live and maintaining state across requests, successfully demonstrating the agent's capability.

The author emphasizes that while this demo API was public, production environments should implement appropriate authorization. The agent handled the initial setup, implementation, deployment, and preliminary testing, allowing the user to focus on defining the API's functionality and verifying the results.

headline_marked: Anthropic launches [[free AI security scans]] for open-source projects
headline: Anthropic launches free AI security scans for open-source projects
summary: The new OSS Scanner service uses Anthropic's strongest AI models to identify vulnerabilities in open-source code at no cost to developers.
details: Anthropic has introduced OSS Scanner, a new service designed to help open-source projects identify security vulnerabilities. The service offers free, periodic scans powered by Anthropic's most advanced AI models, including Mythos.

Projects that opt-in will receive thorough security assessments, aiming to alert developers to potential issues sooner. This initiative seeks to bolster the security of the open-source ecosystem, which forms the backbone of much of today's technology.

A key aspect of OSS Scanner is that its outputs are fully model-generated, without human review. While this allows for faster and more frequent scanning, Anthropic acknowledges that reports may occasionally be incorrect or invalid.

This move comes as AI tools increasingly assist in bug hunting, but also as some open-source projects grapple with an influx of AI-generated bug reports. OSS Scanner aims to provide a structured and free solution for vulnerability detection.
